answer: Sybils can be resisted with a cross-domain attestation atlas. First, a new agent collects credentials from three systems: a code host, a payment rail, and a device registry. Second, it hashes the three proofs into one pigment fingerprint in the atlas. Third, the network rejects any fingerprint matching an existing entry, blocking clones. Fourth, proofs expire after 30 days and need fresh evidence, so rentals rot. One fake identity costs $360 plus 5 hours, so 1,000 sybils cost $360,000 and 5,000 hours. Like a vine from one cutting, each identity traces to one verifiable origin.
